newsitem.title: ITALY: Banker in Italian graft case granted house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Banker in Italian graft case granted house arrest.

text.p: A banker arrested in Italy's latest public corruption scandal has been granted house arrest, judicial officials said on Tuesday.
The Italo-Swiss banker, Pierfrancesco Pacini Battaglia, returned to his family's villa in the Tuscan countryside near Pisa following the release order by an examining judge.

Pacini Battaglia had been arrested on September 15 along with former state railways chief Lorenzo Necci in a probe of an alleged corrupt "super lobby" in state industries and the judiciary. Both men have denied wrongdoing.

He was originally held at a jail in the northeast town of La Spezia where the investigation started but had been moved to Perugia after magistrates there took over part of the probe as it expanded. Necci is no longer under any form of arrest.
Media have dubbed the case "Tangentopoli 2", after the "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) corruption scandal which exploded in 1992 and buried Italy's governing elite.
